sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head and pronotum with moderately dense setae. Head very flat, the sides converging anteriorly; posterior margin trilobate, the middle lobe not very prominent; fontanelle small and round; frontal gland absent. Labrum asymmetrical, curved or wrapping around the mandible bases, ligulate, the sides converging anteriorly into an obtuse point. Mandibles asymmetrical: the left mandible strongly curved at the middle, thick at the base, the outer region ridged and concave, the anterior region spoon-shaped, blunt at the tip, the inner basal tooth long, marginal tooth 3 well developed; the right mandible straight, the posterior margin of marginal tooth 2 straight, an acute angle between teeth 1 and 2. Antennae 14-segmented. Pronotum much narrower than the head, the anterior lobe slightly upturned. Tibial spur formula 2:2:2. Middle tibia specialized, without spines.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Mandibles as in Fig. 46. Left mandible with a small apical tooth, the posterior margin of the fused teeth 1+2 long, marginal tooth 3 well developed; right mandible with the posterior margin of marginal tooth 2 straight, an acute angle between teeth 1 and 2. The alate-worker mandibles are the same as in Neocapritermes.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The genus is most closely related to Neocapritermes and may have been derived from it. The alate-worker mandibles are identical in the two genera; but in Neocapritermes the soldier head is thicker, with the posterior margin evenly rounded or slightly concave at the middle (in this genus the head is very flat and the posterior margin distinctly trilobate), the antennae are 15—16-segmented (14-segmented in this genus), and the pronotum is distinctly saddle-shaped with the anterior lobe markedly upturned.
